title: Kitchener 2051 new Official Plan adopted
subtitle: Fire Station 8 housing project, Dundee Secondary Plan, symphony grant, winter maintenance, pothole technology and heritage designations.
overview: Council adopted the new Kitchener 2051 Official Plan {{vote:m4}}, with site-specific changes allowing drive-through facilities and some auto-related uses at several commercial sites, and a Commercial First designation for 585 Bridgeport Road. It is forwarded to the Province for approval. Council also approved the Dundee Secondary Plan {{vote:m5}} after removing a minimum floor space ratio policy. Amendments to raise housing-mix and density requirements in new greenfield developments were not adopted.

Council accepted the Fire Station 8 and mixed-use housing validation report, conditional on funding for the housing component {{vote:m3}}. It approved a one-time $70,000 grant to the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony with a June 2027 report-back {{vote:m2}}, and let Centre in the Square keep its year-end surpluses and deficits {{vote:m1}}.

Residents will also see winter maintenance and pothole response improvements {{vote:m43}}, a staff study of AI-based pothole monitoring {{vote:m37}}, and more heritage designations. After a closed session, Council authorized a land lease at 450-470 King Street East {{vote:m49}} and a forgivable affordable housing loan {{vote:m48}}. Council also took no further action on designating 24 King Street East {{vote:m40}}.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the new Official Plan as amended, adding site-specific drive-through and auto-use permissions and a Commercial First designation at 585 Bridgeport Road, and forwarded it to the Province {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the Dundee Secondary Plan amendment with the minimum floor space ratio policy deleted, and received the Class Environmental Assessment for filing {{vote:m5}}.
Council accepted the conditional validation report and base target cost, with up to an additional $5m from the Build Community Strong Fund if the fire station proceeds alone {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved a one-time $70,000 grant, required a June 2027 report-back, and asked staff to propose a performance-based funding model tied to earned revenue {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved improvements for extreme winters and pothole response, including contracted surge capacity and doubling road resurfacing funding in 2027 {{vote:m43}}.
Staff will explore AI-based data tools and better resource allocation for pothole repair, reporting back through a future budget discussion {{vote:m37}}.
Council approved a zoning amendment and gave approval under the Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act for a crematorium {{vote:m36}}.
Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a high-rise mixed-use development and endorsed its Urban Design Brief {{vote:m33}}.

debate: On the Official Plan, a delegate for a southwest Kitchener landowner argued that food store and drive-through rules would effectively down-zone existing commercial sites. Councillors responded with site-specific permissions for drive-throughs and auto uses.

One delegate urged adopting the plan as staff recommended, without carve-outs for two neighbourhoods. A resident delegate supported the three-storey height limit outside strategic growth areas in the Auditorium area, saying it still allows gentle intensification.

A delegate asked for 60% non-single-detached housing in large new developments and higher density targets. Staff said the 60% figure had no industry consultation. They also said the density targets follow provincial methodology and the Province could modify higher ones. Both amendments were not adopted.

On Dundee, councillors raised concern that a proposed housing-mix change had not been discussed with affected property owners. Staff confirmed it was not a staff recommendation, and the amendment was later withdrawn.

On the Symphony grant, councillors asked why it should not wait for the 2027 budget and whether the organization is sustainable. The symphony said it would not run deficits, and staff described a conditional funding model with reporting.
